rationale:
Split into three children; each is a genuine, reusable obligation of the supplied proof.

1. covector_det_expansion reuses the accepted, comparator-checked Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_covector_det_expansion. Its frozen type is identical, its status is accepted and it has candidate commit 2c87728a, so the controller's reuse check (_accepted_checkpoint, existing_by_name) passes. It is supplied step 1 (E) in its k!-weighted form over all index maps. Across branches it is available to this node only as a listed child.

2. minor_bound (new, cmcdt_lpi_pc_minor_measurable_bound) is supplied step 2: the minor u ↦ det((DG(u)e_{b t})_{a s}) of an L-Lipschitz G is measurable with absolute value at most r!·L^r. It is used twice: by scalar_continuity (domination and integrability) and by the parent's finite-sum step (integrability of every summand). The accepted dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_minor_measurable_bound cannot replace it. That lemma differentiates scalar component functions, which differs from the coordinates of fderiv where G is not differentiable.

3. scalar_continuity (new, cmcdt_lpi_pc_scalar_weak_continuity; depends on minor_bound) is supplied step 3 (a)–(b) for one index, with a general continuous, compactly supported coefficient f and general rows and columns. Its frozen proof cites cmcdt_lpi_minor_weak_continuity by its exact Lean name. The controller therefore passes this parent's dependency to it as an inherited prerequisite (inherited.py, cited_inherited).

How the children prove the selected statement (supplied steps 1–4). Fix m, N', L, H, H₀, w, ω.
- For I : Fin m → Fin N' let ω_I(y) := ω(y)(e'_{I 0}, …, e'_{I(m−1)}). It is continuous (continuous_eval_const composed with ω). It has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left, because ω(y) = 0 implies ω_I(y) = 0).
- Let M_I(G)(u) := det((DG(u)e_t)_{I s})_{s,t}. This is the children's minor with r := m, a := I, b := fun t => t.
(i) Apply the expansion with f := ω(G u) and u_b := DG(u)e_b, and divide by m! ≠ 0: w(u)·ω(G u)(DG(u)e) = (m!)⁻¹·Σ_I w(u)·(ω_I(G u)·M_I(G)(u)). This is (E') with the strictly increasing J replaced by all I. Each J is hit by the m! maps J∘π, whose terms are equal, and non-injective I contribute 0. Since minor_continuity allows any rows a, no regrouping is needed.
(ii) For G ∈ {H_j, H₀}, minor_bound and the boundedness of ω_I make every summand integrable (Integrable.mul_bdd). Hence ∫ w·ω(G)(DG e) = (m!)⁻¹·Σ_I ∫ w·(ω_I∘G)·M_I(G) (integral_const_mul, integral_finsetSum).
(iii) scalar_continuity with p := N', r := m, a := I, b := fun t => t and f := ω_I gives convergence of every summand. This is T1_j + T2_j → 0 of supplied step 3.
(iv) tendsto_finsetSum and Tendsto.const_mul finish the proof. The cases m = 0 and N' < m need no special treatment.

subproblems.title: Coordinate expansion of a covector, k!-weighted over all index maps (reuses accepted dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_covector_det_expansion)
subproblems.statement: Let N', k ∈ ℕ, let f be a k-covector on ℝ^{N'} (a continuous alternating k-linear form, Covector (Euclid N') k), and let u = (u_0, …, u_{k−1}) ∈ (ℝ^{N'})^k. Write e'_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i ∈ Fin N'. Then k!·f(u) = Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin N'} f(e'_{I(0)}, …, e'_{I(k−1)})·det(u_b(I(c)))_{c,b ∈ Fin k}, where the sum runs over all maps I : Fin k → Fin N'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N' k : ℕ) (f : Covector (Euclid N') k) (u : Fin k → Euclid N'), (k.factorial : ℝ) * f u = ∑ I : Fin k → Fin N', f (fun c => EuclideanSpace.single (I c) (1 : ℝ)) * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => u b (I c))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused verbatim: this is the accepted, comparator-checked declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_covector_det_expansion (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.flat_convergence-a1.deformation-a1.jacobian_weak_continuity-a1.covector_det_expansion-a1, candidate commit 2c87728aa7637a3a07953c178f3e4f9547979008). Its frozen Lean type is identical, and its accepted proof (steps 1–7 below) is copied verbatim. In the selected parent it replaces step 1 (E). Each strictly increasing J arises from exactly k! maps I = J∘π (π a permutation), and their terms coincide: f(e'∘J∘π) = sign(π)·f(e'∘J), and permuting the rows multiplies the determinant by sign(π). Non-injective I contribute 0. So this identity is (E) multiplied by k!.

Notation. ℝ^{N'} = Euclid N'; e'_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N'); z(i) (Lean z i) is the i-th coordinate of z ∈ ℝ^{N'}. For I : Fin k → Fin N' put e'_I := (e'_{I(0)}, …, e'_{I(k−1)}) and let M_I be the k×k matrix with (M_I)_{c,b} = u_b(I(c)).

1. (Basis expansion.) Every z ∈ ℝ^{N'} satisfies z = Σ_{i ∈ Fin N'} z(i)·e'_i (the standard basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun has the coordinates as its repr; Basis.sum_repr). In particular u_b = Σ_i u_b(i)·e'_i for every b.
2. (Multilinear expansion.) f is multilinear, so (MultilinearMap.map_sum) f(u) = f(Σ_i u_0(i)e'_i, …, Σ_i u_{k−1}(i)e'_i) = Σ_{J : Fin k → Fin N'} f(u_0(J 0)·e'_{J 0}, …, u_{k−1}(J(k−1))·e'_{J(k−1)}), and pulling out the scalars (MultilinearMap.map_smul_univ) each summand equals (Π_b u_b(J b))·f(e'_J). Hence f(u) = Σ_J (Π_b u_b(J b))·f(e'_J).
3. (Reindexing by a permutation.) Fix σ ∈ Perm(Fin k). The map I ↦ I ∘ σ is a bijection of the finite set of maps Fin k → Fin N' (inverse J ↦ J ∘ σ⁻¹; Lean Equiv.arrowCongr σ⁻¹ (Equiv.refl _)). Substituting J = I ∘ σ in step 2: f(u) = Σ_I (Π_b u_b(I(σ b)))·f(e'_{I(σ 0)}, …, e'_{I(σ(k−1))}).
4. (Alternation.) The family (e'_{I(σ b)})_b is the family e'_I composed with σ, and an alternating map satisfies f(v ∘ σ) = sign(σ)·f(v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Hence, for every σ, f(u) = Σ_I sign(σ)·(Π_b u_b(I(σ b)))·f(e'_I).
5. (Averaging.) Perm(Fin k) has k! elements (Fintype.card_perm). Summing step 4 over all σ and exchanging the two finite sums: k!·f(u) = Σ_σ f(u) = Σ_I f(e'_I)·Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b u_b(I(σ b)).
6. (Leibniz formula.) By Matrix.det_apply, det M_I = Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b (M_I)_{σ(b), b} = Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b u_b(I(σ b)). Substituting into step 5 gives k!·f(u) = Σ_I f(e'_I)·det M_I, the claim.
7. (Degenerate cases.) Steps 1–6 use neither k ≥ 1 nor N' ≥ 1. For k = 0 there is exactly one I (the empty map), 0! = 1, the empty determinant is 1 and f(e'_I) = f(u) (both arguments are the empty family). For N' = 0 < k the right side is an empty sum and step 2 gives f(u) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Expand each u_b in the standard basis and use multilinearity: f(u) = Σ_J (Π_b u_b(J b))·f(e'_J).
For each permutation σ reindex J = I ∘ σ and use alternation f(v ∘ σ) = sign(σ) f(v).
Average over the k! permutations and exchange the finite sums.
Recognize Σ_σ sign(σ) Π_b u_b(I(σ b)) as det(u_b(I_c))_{c,b} by the Leibniz formula.

subproblems.title: Jacobian minors of a Lipschitz map are measurable and bounded by r!·L^r
subproblems.statement: Let m, p, r ∈ ℕ and L ≥ 0, let v : ℝ^m → ℝ^p be L-Lipschitz, and let a : Fin r → Fin p (rows) and b : Fin r → Fin m (columns). For u ∈ ℝ^m put M(u) := det((Dv(u)e_{b(t)})_{a(s)})_{s,t ∈ Fin r}. Here Dv(u) := fderiv ℝ v u (the zero map where v is not differentiable), and e_t := EuclideanSpace.single t 1 is the standard basis of ℝ^m. Then M is (Borel) measurable on ℝ^m, and |M(u)| ≤ r!·L^r for every u ∈ ℝ^m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m p r : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (v : Euclid m → Euclid p) (a : Fin r → Fin p) (b : Fin r → Fin m), LipschitzWith L v → Measurable (fun u => Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun s t => fderiv ℝ v u (EuclideanSpace.single (b t) 1) (a s))) ∧ ∀ u, |Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun s t => fderiv ℝ v u (EuclideanSpace.single (b t) 1) (a s))| ≤ (r.factorial : ℝ) * (L : ℝ) ^ r
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (bounds and measurability) of the supplied proof of the selected parent, cmcdt_lpi_pullback_weak_continuity. Here it is stated for one Lipschitz map with arbitrary rows a and columns b; the parent uses r := m, a := I and b := id.

Notation. Dv(u) := fderiv ℝ v u ∈ L(ℝ^m, ℝ^p), with the operator norm ‖·‖. e_t := EuclideanSpace.single t 1 ∈ ℝ^m, so ‖e_t‖ = 1. y_i is the i-th coordinate of y ∈ ℝ^p. For a continuous linear map A : ℝ^m → ℝ^p let Φ(A) be the r×r matrix with entries Φ(A)_{s,t} := (A e_{b(t)})_{a(s)}. Then M(u) = det Φ(Dv(u)).

1. (Measurability of the derivative.) ℝ^m and ℝ^p are finite-dimensional and ℝ^p is complete. So u ↦ Dv(u) is Borel measurable from ℝ^m to L(ℝ^m, ℝ^p) for every function v (Mathlib measurable_fderiv; no regularity of v is needed).
2. (Continuity of A ↦ det Φ(A).) Fix s, t. The entry A ↦ (A e_{b(t)})_{a(s)} is the evaluation A ↦ A e_{b(t)} (continuous: evaluation at a fixed vector, continuous_eval_const) followed by the coordinate y ↦ y_{a(s)} (the continuous linear functional EuclideanSpace.proj (a s)). Hence A ↦ Φ(A) is continuous into Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℝ with the product topology (continuous_pi in both indices). The determinant is a polynomial in the entries, so A ↦ det Φ(A) is continuous (Continuous.matrix_det).
3. (Measurability of M.) M is the continuous map A ↦ det Φ(A) composed with the measurable map u ↦ Dv(u). Hence M is measurable. This is the first conjunct.
4. (Entry bound.) Fix u ∈ ℝ^m. Since v is L-Lipschitz, ‖Dv(u)‖ ≤ L (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; where v is not differentiable, Dv(u) = 0). For all s, t:
   |Φ(Dv(u))_{s,t}| = |(Dv(u)e_{b(t)})_{a(s)}| ≤ ‖Dv(u)e_{b(t)}‖ ≤ ‖Dv(u)‖·‖e_{b(t)}‖ = ‖Dv(u)‖ ≤ L.
   The first inequality holds because each coordinate of a Euclidean vector is bounded by its norm (PiLp.norm_apply_le). The second is the operator-norm bound (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm).
5. (Leibniz bound.) Let A be a real r×r matrix and x ∈ ℝ with |A_{i,j}| ≤ x for all i, j.
   - By the Leibniz formula (Matrix.det_apply), det A = Σ_{σ ∈ Perm(Fin r)} sign(σ)·Π_i A_{σ(i), i}.
   - By the triangle inequality, and because sign(σ) = ±1, |det A| ≤ Σ_σ Π_i |A_{σ(i),i}|.
   - Each factor satisfies 0 ≤ |A_{σ(i),i}| ≤ x, so each product is at most x^r (finite products of nonnegative numbers are monotone).
   - There are r! permutations (Fintype.card_perm, with card (Fin r) = r). Hence |det A| ≤ r!·x^r.
6. (Conclusion.) Step 4 allows step 5 with A := Φ(Dv(u)) and x := L. This gives |M(u)| ≤ r!·L^r for every u, the second conjunct. Together with step 3 this proves the claim. For r = 0 the matrix is empty and det = 1 = 0!·L^0, which is also what step 5 gives. ∎
proof_key_steps: u ↦ fderiv ℝ v u is Borel (measurable_fderiv), and A ↦ det((A e_{b t})_{a s}) is continuous, so the minor is measurable.
Each entry satisfies |(Dv(u)e_{b t})_{a s}| ≤ ‖Dv(u)‖ ≤ L (coordinate ≤ norm, operator norm, norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
Leibniz formula with |sign σ| = 1 and r! permutations gives |det| ≤ r!·L^r.

subproblems.title: Weak continuity of f(v_j)·(Jacobian minor of v_j) against L¹ weights, for continuous compactly supported f
subproblems.statement: Let m, p, r ∈ ℕ and L ≥ 0. Let v_j, v₀ : ℝ^m → ℝ^p (j ∈ ℕ) be L-Lipschitz maps with v_j → v₀ uniformly on ℝ^m. Let a : Fin r → Fin p and b : Fin r → Fin m, let w ∈ L¹(ℝ^m) (Lebesgue), and let f : ℝ^p → ℝ be continuous with compact support. For a map v put M(v)(u) := det((Dv(u)e_{b(t)})_{a(s)})_{s,t ∈ Fin r}, with Dv(u) := fderiv ℝ v u and e_t := EuclideanSpace.single t 1. Then ∫ w(u)·(f(v_j(u))·M(v_j)(u)) du → ∫ w(u)·(f(v₀(u))·M(v₀)(u)) du as j → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m p r : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (v : ℕ → Euclid m → Euclid p) (v₀ : Euclid m → Euclid p) (a : Fin r → Fin p) (b : Fin r → Fin m) (w : Euclid m → ℝ) (f : Euclid p → ℝ), (∀ j, LipschitzWith L (v j)) → LipschitzWith L v₀ → TendstoUniformly v v₀ atTop → Integrable w → Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ u, w u * (f (v j u) * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun s t => fderiv ℝ (v j) u (EuclideanSpace.single (b t) 1) (a s)))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ u, w u * (f (v₀ u) * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun s t => fderiv ℝ v₀ u (EuclideanSpace.single (b t) 1) (a s)))))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 (a)–(b) of the supplied proof of the selected parent, cmcdt_lpi_pullback_weak_continuity. These are the two terms T1_j and T2_j for one fixed index. Here ω_J is replaced by a general continuous, compactly supported f, and the minor is taken with general rows a and columns b.

Prerequisites.
- The sibling minor_bound, Lean name cmcdt_lpi_pc_minor_measurable_bound: for an L-Lipschitz G : ℝ^m → ℝ^p, the function u ↦ det((DG(u)e_{b(t)})_{a(s)})_{s,t} is measurable, and its absolute value is at most r!·L^r everywhere.
- The selected parent's dependency minor_continuity, Lean name cmcdt_lpi_minor_weak_continuity. Its frozen statement: let v_j, v₀ be L-Lipschitz with v_j → v₀ uniformly, let a be rows and b columns, and let c : ℝ^m → ℝ be Lebesgue-integrable. Then ∫ c(u)·det((Dv_j(u)e_{b(t)})_{a(s)}) du → ∫ c(u)·det((Dv₀(u)e_{b(t)})_{a(s)}) du.

Notation. λ := volume on ℝ^m. M_j := M(v_j) and M₀ := M(v₀). K := r!·L^r ≥ 0. W := ∫|w| dλ < ∞.

1. (Bounds.)
   - Apply cmcdt_lpi_pc_minor_measurable_bound, with the same a and b, to each v_j and to v₀ (all are L-Lipschitz). So M_j and M₀ are measurable, and |M_j(u)| ≤ K and |M₀(u)| ≤ K for all u.
   - f is continuous with compact support, so it is bounded: there is C with |f(y)| ≤ C for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). It is also uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous).
   - Lipschitz maps are continuous, so f∘v_j and f∘v₀ are continuous.
2. (Integrability.) Let g : ℝ^m → ℝ be continuous with |g| ≤ D, and let G be L-Lipschitz.
   - g·M(G) is measurable (a continuous function times a measurable one), and |g·M(G)| ≤ D·K by step 1 applied to G.
   - Hence u ↦ w(u)·(g(u)·M(G)(u)) is integrable: an integrable function times a bounded, a.e.-strongly-measurable function is integrable (Integrable.mul_bdd).
   - In the same way c := w·(f∘v₀) is integrable, since |f∘v₀| ≤ C.
   - In particular, for every j the following two functions are integrable:
     - u ↦ w(u)·((f(v_j u) − f(v₀ u))·M_j(u)) (take g := f∘v_j − f∘v₀, D := 2C, G := v_j);
     - u ↦ c(u)·M_j(u) = w(u)·(f(v₀ u)·M_j(u)) (take g := f∘v₀, D := C, G := v_j).
3. (Splitting.) For every j and u, w(u)·(f(v_j u)·M_j(u)) = w(u)·((f(v_j u) − f(v₀ u))·M_j(u)) + c(u)·M_j(u). Integrate, using step 2 and additivity of the integral: ∫ w·(f∘v_j)·M_j = T1_j + S_j, where
   - T1_j := ∫ w·(f∘v_j − f∘v₀)·M_j,
   - S_j := ∫ c·M_j.
   Also w(u)·(f(v₀ u)·M₀(u)) = c(u)·M₀(u) pointwise, so ∫ w·(f∘v₀)·M₀ = 0 + ∫ c·M₀.
4. (T1_j → 0.)
   - f is uniformly continuous and v_j → v₀ uniformly, so f∘v_j → f∘v₀ uniformly on ℝ^m (UniformContinuous.comp_tendstoUniformly).
   - Let ε > 0 and put η := ε/(2(KW + 1)) > 0. There is j₀ such that |f(v_j(u)) − f(v₀(u))| < η for all j ≥ j₀ and all u.
   - For such j and every u, |w(u)·(f(v_j u) − f(v₀ u))·M_j(u)| ≤ |w(u)|·η·K, and u ↦ ηK|w(u)| is integrable.
   - So |T1_j| ≤ ∫ ηK|w| dλ = ηK·W ≤ η(KW + 1) = ε/2 < ε (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le).
   Hence T1_j → 0.
5. (S_j → ∫ c·M₀.) Apply cmcdt_lpi_minor_weak_continuity with:
   - the same m, p, r and L;
   - the maps v := (v_j)_j and v₀ (L-Lipschitz, with v_j → v₀ uniformly);
   - rows a and columns b;
   - the integrable weight c from step 2.
   Its matrix entry fderiv ℝ (v j) u (EuclideanSpace.single (b t) 1) (a s) is (Dv_j(u)e_{b(t)})_{a(s)}, the (s,t) entry of the matrix of M_j(u). So it gives S_j = ∫ c·M_j → ∫ c·M₀.
6. (Conclusion.) A sum of convergent sequences converges to the sum of the limits. By steps 3–5, ∫ w·(f∘v_j)·M_j = T1_j + S_j → 0 + ∫ c·M₀ = ∫ w·(f∘v₀)·M₀. ∎
proof_key_steps: The minors M(v_j), M(v₀) are measurable and bounded by r!·L^r (cmcdt_lpi_pc_minor_measurable_bound); f is bounded and uniformly continuous.
All integrands are integrable (L¹ weight times bounded measurable); split ∫ w·f(v_j)·M_j = T1_j + ∫ c·M_j with c := w·f(v₀).
T1_j → 0: f∘v_j → f∘v₀ uniformly, so eventually |T1_j| ≤ η·K·‖w‖₁ < ε.
∫ c·M_j → ∫ c·M₀ by cmcdt_lpi_minor_weak_continuity with the integrable weight c; add the two limits.
